STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.claim: The surah opens by describing the virtues and righteous actions of believers.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.anchor: begins by describing the virtues and righteous actions of those who believe

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r1.claim: Khushūʿ means humility and meekness, not merely comfort; Qur'anic uses about lowered voices and submissive hearts show its essence as full inward submission expressed in posture, recitation, and prostration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r1.anchor: The word ﺧﺸﻮعۡmeans “humility and meekness.” It has been used in the Qur’ ān in different forms.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r2.claim: The previous sūrah stressed diligence in the prayer's outward form; this sūrah highlights its inner essence as an attribute of the believers promised success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p239/r2.anchor: This signifies diligence in the outer form of the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.claim: Al-Mu'minūn's opening describes success through humble prayer, avoiding frivolity, zakāh, chastity and restraint, trustworthiness, and keeping promises.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.anchor: salvation and success before God is reserved for those believers whose prayers are marked with humility and concentration

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r9.claim: خشوع linguistically means submission and humility.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r10.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r10.claim: Amr ibn Dinar defines prayer's humility as stillness and a dignified bearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r10.anchor: قال عمرو بن دينار: هو السكون وحسن الهيئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r11.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r11.claim: Mujahid defines it as lowering the gaze and showing humility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: غض البصر وخفض الجناح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r12.speaker: مسلم بن يسار وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r12.claim: Muslim ibn Yasar and Qatada define it as bowing the head.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r12.anchor: وقال مسلم بن يسار وقتادة: تنكيس الرأس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r14.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak defines it as placing the right hand over the left.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r14.anchor: وقال الضحاك: وضع اليمين على الشمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r15.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r15.claim: Ali defines it as not turning during prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r15.anchor: وعن علي: ترك الالتفات في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r16.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r16.claim: Abu al-Darda defines it as revering the standing place, speaking sincerely, possessing full certainty, and gathering one's attention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r16.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء: إعظام المقام وإخلاص المقال واليقين التام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r17.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r17.claim: A report says the Prophet used to pray with his gaze raised toward the sky; after this verse was revealed, he directed his gaze toward the place of prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r17.anchor: وفي الحديث أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يصلي رافعا بصره إلى السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r18.claim: Prayerful humility includes proper manners: avoiding gathered-up clothes, fidgeting with the body or clothes, turning, stretching, yawning, closing the eyes, covering the mouth, trailing garments, cracking or interlacing fingers, standing with hands on hips, and moving pebbles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r18.anchor: ومن الخشوع أن تستعمل الآداب فيتوقى كف الثوب والعبث بجسده وثيابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r19.speaker: التحرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r19.claim: Al-Tahrir reports disagreement over whether humility is obligatory or a meritorious completion of prayer, and judges the first view correct; its locus is the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r19.anchor: التحرير: اختلف في الخشوع، هل هو من فرائض الصلاة أو من فضائلها ومكملاتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r20.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r20.claim: Ubada ibn al-Samit says humility is the first knowledge taken away from people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p546/r20.anchor: وهو أول علم يرفع من الناس قاله عبادة بن الصامت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r1.claim: Prayer is attributed to worshippers because they alone benefit from it; it is their provision and store, while God has no need of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r1.anchor: فالمصلي هو المنتفع بها وحده وهي عدته وذخيرته فهي صلاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r6.claim: Humility and guarding prayer differ: humility combines inward vigilance and bodily submission, while guarding means regular performance on time, with purity, conditions, and sound fulfillment of the pillars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r6.anchor: والخشوع والمحافظة متغايران بدأ أولا بالخشوع وهو الجامع للمراقبة القلبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the initial singular as prayer in its generic sense and the later plural as guarding the counted prayers, including obligatory prayers and many regular or optional services.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p549/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ووحدت أولا ليفاد الخشوع في جنس الصلاة أي صلاة كانت، وجمعت آخرا لتفاد المحافظة على أعدادها

SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase is placed before its complement for emphasis; the pause at the verse ending makes this order apt, as in the following parallel verses.
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r1.anchor: الجار متعلق بما بعده وقدم للاهتمام، وحسنه كون متعلقه فاصلة، وكذلك فيما بعده

SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r2.claim: Prayer is attributed to the worshippers because they benefit from it, whereas the one prayed to has no need of it.
SAMIN-DURR:23:2/r2.anchor: وأضيفت الصلاة إليه لأنهم هم المنتفعون بها، والمصلى له غني عنها، فلذلك أضيفت

SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the first singular denotes prayer in general, while the final plural denotes preserving the five prayers, witr, and regular sunnas.
SAMIN-DURR:23:8/r7.anchor: ثم قال: " وأيضا فقد وحدت أولا

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r5.claim: The lexical basis of خشوع is submission and humility, illustrated by the voices becoming subdued before the Merciful in 20:108.
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r5.anchor: أصل الخشوع في اللغة الخضوع والتواضع، ودليل ذلك قوله:

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatāda explain خاشعون as fearful.

ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r7.speaker: النبي
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet used to raise his gaze toward heaven when standing in prayer, then after this verse was revealed he looked toward his place of prostration.
ZAJJAJ:v4p5/r7.anchor: وروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه كان إذا وقف في صلاته رفع بصره نحو السماء،

ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.claim: Believers attain a happy state through humility in prayer and active pursuit of inner purity.
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.anchor: TRULY, to a happy state shall attain the believe rs: (23:2) those who humble themselves

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.claim: The Qur’an associates believers’ khushūʿ with worship in worldly life, citing the believers’ prayer, the faithful People of the Book, and earlier prophets.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r1.anchor: آل عمران 199: {خَاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.claim: When criminals, disbelievers, or wrongdoers are described as humble, the context is the afterlife and the humiliation of judgment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r2.anchor: فإذا جاء الخشوع، في البيان القرآني من المجرمين والكفار، فذلك إنما يكون منهم في اليوم الآخر الذي كانوا يوعدون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.claim: She highlights the rhetorical contrast: believers show khushūʿ toward God in this life, while disbelievers and wrongdoers show it only in the hereafter.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p228/r3.anchor: وأمعن التدبر لهاذ الملحظ من المراد مجئ خشوع المؤمنين لله في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r1.claim: The nominal خاشعون conveys enduring humility in prayer, not a passing moment; it should last in heart and limbs throughout prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r1.anchor: جاء بالخشوع بالصيغة الاسمية الدالة على الثبات ولم يقل: (يخشعون) للدلالة على أنه وصف لهم دائم في الصلاة غير عارض

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r2.claim: Fronting في صلاتهم signals care and gives prayer priority as Islam’s most important pillar.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r2.anchor: وتقديم الجار والمجرور (في صلاتهم) على (خاشعون) له دلالته أيضاً، ذلك أن التقديم يفيد العناية والاهتمام، فقدَّمَ الصلاةَ لأنها أَهمُّ ركنٍ في الإسلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r3.speaker: unspecified
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r3.claim: The author cites a sound report calling the one who abandons prayer a disbeliever and destroyer of religion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r3.anchor: جاء في الأثر الصحيح، أن تاركها كافر هادم للدين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r4.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r4.claim: Some jurists hold that one who abandons prayer is an unbeliever even if he has pronounced the two testimonies.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r4.anchor: وحتى أن الفقهاء اختلفوا في كفر تاركها فمنهم من قال: إن تاركها كافر وإنْ نطق بالشهادتين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r5.claim: Prayer without humility still fulfills the obligation and pillar; a non-praying person has not done so.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r5.anchor: والصلاةُ من غير خشوع أكبرُ وأعظم عند الله من خشوعٍ بلا صلاة، فإن المصلي، وإن لم يكن خاشعاً أسقط فرضه وقام بركنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r6.claim: Humility is a bodily and inward quality found inside or outside prayer and can describe nonhuman things, as with humble voices.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p132/r6.anchor: إن الخشوع وَصْفٌ قلبي وجسمي، يكون في الصلاة وغيرها، ويوصف به الإنسان وغيره. قال تعالى: {وَخَشَعَتِ الأصوات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r1.claim: In al-Muʾminūn, khushūʿ is broader than persistence in prayer: it includes persistence plus inward and bodily attentiveness, and the worshipper remains absorbed until finishing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r1.anchor: والخشوع أعَمُّ من الدوام ذلك أنه يشمل الدوام على الصلاة وزيادة فهو روحُ الصلاة، وهو من أفعالِ القلوب والجوارح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r1.speaker: الزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri defines humility in prayer as a person’s stillness during prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r1.anchor: عن الزهري في قوله ﴿ في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ قال هو سكون المرء في صلاته

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the worshippers are fearful.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r3.claim: Qatada locates humility in the heart.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r3.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وقال قتادة الخشوع في القلب

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r4.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r4.claim: Ali says humility means not turning around during prayer and softening one’s shoulders toward a fellow Muslim.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p43#2/r4.anchor: عن علي قال سئل عن قوله ﴿ الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ قال لا تلتفت في صلاتك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r1.claim: The verse's attributes either distinguish the true believers, or—if they also follow faith's branches—clarify or praise them; some reports support the restrictive analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r1.anchor: وما عطف عليه صفات مخصصة لهم وإما الآتون بفروعه أيضا كما بنبيء إضافة الصلاة إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the possessive phrase their prayer to indicate that the worshipers benefit from prayer, not the One worshiped.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الإضافة للإشارة إلى أنهم هم المنتفعون بالصلاة دون المصلى له عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r3.claim: Khushūʿ is humble submission with fear and bodily stillness.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r3.anchor: والخشوع التذلل مع خوف وسكون للجوارح ولذا قال ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the humble as fearful and still.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس فيما رواه عنه ابن جرير وغيره خاشعون خائفون ساكنون

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid explains khushūʿ here as lowering the gaze and showing humility.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه هنا غض البصر وخفض الجناح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r6.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r6.claim: Muslim ibn Yasār and Qatāda interpret khushūʿ as bowing the head.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r6.anchor: وقال مسلم بن يسار وقتادة : تنكيس الرأس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī explains khushūʿ as refraining from turning around during prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r7.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه ترك الإلتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets khushūʿ as placing the right hand over the left.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك : وضع اليمين على الشمال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r9.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ describes khushūʿ as revering the presence, speaking sincerely, possessing full certainty, and giving complete attention.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r9.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء إعظام المقام وإخلاص المقال واليقين التام وجميع الإهتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r10.claim: Turning away in prayer is a satanic theft from the worshiper's prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r10.anchor: ويتبع ذلك ترك الإلتفات وهو من الشيطان فقد روى البخاري وأبو داود

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r11.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r11.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet called turning during prayer a theft by which Satan steals from a servant's prayer; the report is in al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Nasāʾī.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r11.anchor: فقد روى البخاري وأبو داود والنسائي عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : سألت رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r12.claim: Abū Hurayra recalls a Prophetic instruction that no one turn during prayer; if unavoidable, the turning should not concern what God made obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن أبي هريرة أنه قال في مرضه : أقعدوني أقعدوني فإن عندي وديعة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r13.claim: Khushūʿ also entails leaving bodily and clothing fidgeting; denying that such behavior conflicts with khushūʿ is, in Al-Ālūsī's view, untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r13.anchor: وترك العبث بثيابه أو شيء من جسده وإنكار منافاته مكابرة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r14.claim: A weak report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet saw a man playing with his beard in prayer and said that a humble heart would make the limbs humble too.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r14.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه رأى رجلا يعبث بلحيته

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r15.claim: Raising the eyes toward heaven during prayer is prohibited, including for a blind worshiper.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r15.anchor: وترك رفع البصر إلى السماء وإن كان المصلي أعمى وقد جاء النهي عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r16.speaker: جابر بن سمرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r16.claim: Jābir ibn Samura reports the Prophet warning that people who raise their eyes to heaven in prayer must stop or their sight may not return; cited by Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and Ibn Mājah.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r16.anchor: فقد أخرج مسلم وأبو داود وابن ماجة عن جابر بن سمرة قال قال النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : لينتهين أقوام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r17.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r17.claim: A report graded sound by al-Ḥākim says the Prophet used to raise his eyes heavenward in prayer before this verse was revealed, then lowered his head.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r17.anchor: فقد أخرج الحاكم وصححه وابن مردوية والبيهقي في سننه عن محمد بن سيرين عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r18.claim: Placing the hand on the hip (ikhtiṣār) in prayer is considered disliked; the report calling it the rest of the people of Hell means it was a Jewish practice, not that Hell offers rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r18.anchor: وترك الإختصار وهو وضع اليد على الخاصرة وقد ذكروا أنه مكروه وجاء عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم الإختصار في الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r19.claim: The cited phrase about rest of the people of Hell means Jews rested this way in prayer and are people of Hell; Hell itself gives no respite.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r19.anchor: أي إن فعل اليهود في صلاتهم استراحة وهم أهل النار لا أن لهم فيها راحة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r20.claim: Swaying in prayer is also prohibited as a Jewish practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#2/r20.anchor: ومن أفعالهم أيضا فيها التميل وقد جاء النهي عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r1.speaker: أم رومان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r1.claim: Umm Rūmān reports that Abū Bakr stopped her swaying in prayer and cited the Prophet's instruction to keep the limbs still, not sway like Jews; bodily stillness completes prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r1.anchor: أخرج الحكيم الترمذي من طريق القاسم بن محمد عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر عن أم رومان والدة عائشة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī includes proper manners in khushūʿ: avoid bunching clothes, stretching, yawning, closing the eyes, covering the mouth, letting garments hang, cracking knuckles, interlacing fingers, and shifting pebbles.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r2.anchor: وقال في الكشاف : من الخشوع أن يستعمل الآداب وذكر من ذلك توقي كف الثوب والتمطي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r3.speaker: التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r3.claim: Al-Taḥrīr reports disagreement over whether khushūʿ is obligatory in prayer or a virtue completing it, and calls the obligatory view correct, locating it in the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r3.anchor: اختلف في الخشوع هل هو من فرائض الصلاة أو من فضائلها ومكملاتها على قولين والصحيح الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the view that inward khushūʿ is a component of valid prayer: it is a condition for acceptance, not performance; some jurists nevertheless make it a validity condition for part of prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r4.anchor: والصحيح عندنا خلافه نعم الحق أنه شرط القبول لا الأجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r5.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r5.claim: Ibn Ḥajar's commentary on al-Minhāj treats khushūʿ throughout prayer as recommended inwardly and outwardly, including not attending to distractions and not moving the limbs without purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r5.anchor: وفي المنهاج وشرحه لابن حجر ويسن الخشوع في كل صلاته بقلبه بأن لا يحضر فيه غير ما هو فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī understands the verse to include both inward and outward khushūʿ; he says the claim that prayer receives no reward without it is supported by sound hadiths.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r6.anchor: وفي الآية المراد كل منهما كما هو ظاهر أيضا وكان سنة لثناء الله تعالى في كتابه العزيز

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r7.claim: For those who treat khushūʿ as a condition of validity in some portion of prayer, prolonged inner distraction and unnecessary fidgeting are disliked; some say prohibited, except for need or securing a benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r7.anchor: ولأن لنا وجها اختاره جمع أنه شرط للصحة لكن في البعض فيكره الإسترسال مع حديث النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r8.claim: Explanations for fronting في صلاتهم include rhyme, bringing prayer beside faith because prayer is called faith elsewhere, or restriction to all of their prayers rather than some.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r8.anchor: وتقديم الظرف قيل لرعاية الفواصل وقيل ليقرب ذكر الصلاة من ذكر الإيمان فإنهما إخوان

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r9.claim: Mentioning khushūʿ first among the believers' qualities honors its importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r9.anchor: وفي تقديم وصفهم بالخشوع في الصلاة على سائر ما يذكر بعد ما لا يخفى من التنويه بشأن الخشوع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r10.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r10.claim: A report al-Ḥākim graded sound from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit predicts that people will enter the mosque and find no humble man; khushūʿ is the first thing lifted from people.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r10.anchor: وجاء أن الخشوع أول ما يرفع من الناس ففي خبر رواه الحاكم وصححه أن عبادة بن الصامت

ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r11.speaker: حذيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r11.claim: A report al-Ḥākim graded sound from Ḥudhayfa says khushūʿ is the first thing lost from religion and prayer the last, as Islam's bonds unravel one by one.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p3#3/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وأحمد في الزهد والحاكم وصححه عن حذيفة قال : أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الخشوع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.claim: ʿUmar reports that revelation sounded like a buzzing bee near the Prophet’s face; after a pause the Prophet faced the qibla, raised his hands, prayed for generous divine favor, and said that whoever establishes ten verses beginning with this opening will enter the Garden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد القارئ قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: كان إذا نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل وعلي بن المديني وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, and others transmit a variant prayer wording that adds a request to be made content, alongside the request for God’s pleasure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.anchor: ورواه أحمد بن حنبل، وعلي ابن المديني، وجماعة عن عبد الرزاق، وقالوا: "وأعطنا ولا تحرمنا وأرضنا وارض عنا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets khushu as humble submission and abasement.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret khushu as fearfulness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets khushu as lowering the gaze and voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو غض البصر وخفض الصوت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r9.claim: Khushu is close to bodily submission, but includes the heart, body, gaze, and voice, whereas submission concerns the body.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r9.anchor: والخشوع قريب من الخضوع إلا أن الخضوع في البدن، والخشوع في القلب والبدن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r10.claim: The phrase about voices becoming humble before the Merciful is cited to illustrate khushu of the voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r10.anchor: قال الله عز وجل: "وخشعت الأصوات للرحمن" (طه -108)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r11.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r11.claim: Ali explains prayerful khushu as not turning to the right or left.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r11.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه: هو أن لا يلتفت يمينا ولا شمالا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r12.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes such absorption that one does not notice those to either side or turn from reverence for God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r12.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو أن لا يعرف من على يمينه ولا من على يساره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r13.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r13.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet called turning during prayer a theft Satan steals from a worshipper's prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r13.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الالتفات في الصلاة فقال: "هو اختلاس يختلسه الشيطان من صلاة العبد"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r14.speaker: أبو ذر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r14.claim: Abu Dharr reports that God remains turned toward a worshipper during prayer but turns away when the worshipper turns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r14.anchor: عن أبي ذر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يزال الله مقبلا على العبد ما كان في صلاته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r15.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r15.claim: Amr ibn Dinar interprets khushu as stillness and good composure.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r15.anchor: وقال عمرو بن دينار: هو السكون وحسن الهيئة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r16.speaker: ابن سيرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r16.claim: Ibn Sirin and others say the worshipper does not raise the gaze from the place of prostration.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r16.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين وغيره: هو أن لا ترفع بصرك عن موضع سجودك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r17.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r17.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Companions lowered their eyes to the prostration place after this verse was revealed, having previously looked toward heaven in prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p405#3/r17.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r16.claim: Prayer is mentioned again to show that preserving it is obligatory just as humility within it is obligatory.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p410/r16.anchor: كرر ذكر الصلاة ليبين أن المحافظة عليها واجبة كما أن الخشوع فيها واجب

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r1.claim: Khushūʿ is reverent fear and humility before God, with the gaze held at the place of prostration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r1.anchor: خائفون من الله سبحانه وتعالى متذللون له ملزمون أبصارهم مساجدهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r2.claim: The Prophet used to pray looking toward the sky; after this verse was revealed, he turned his gaze toward his place of prostration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r2.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي رافعا بصره إلى السماء، فلما نزلت رمى ببصره نحو مسجده

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r3.claim: Seeing a man play with his beard, the Prophet said that if his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble too.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:2/r3.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي رافعا بصره إلى السماء، فلما نزلت رمى ببصره نحو مسجده وأنه رأى رجلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r7.claim: The prayer is ascribed to believers to encourage guarding it: it is between them and God, who has no need of it, while they benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r7.anchor: أضيفت إليهم ترغيبا لهم في حفظها , لأها بينهم وبين الله تعالى , وهو غني عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r8.claim: Khushūʿ is humility, stillness, modesty, and composure, turning inward and outward attention wholly to prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r8.anchor: أي أذلاء ساكنون متواضعون مطمئنون قاصرون بواطنهم وظواهرهم على ما هم فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r9.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī describes reverential fear as disciplining heart, morals, and limbs, including lowering the gaze toward the prostration place from fear that prayer may be rejected.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r9.anchor: قال الرازيك خائفون خوفا يملأ القلب حرمة , والأخلاق تهذيبا , والأطراف تأديبا , أي خشية أن ترد عليهم صلاتهم , ومن ذلك خفض البضر إلى موضع السجود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r10.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī says prayerful attentiveness is alert submission that also shapes conduct in dealings, service, and inward reverence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r10.anchor: قال الرازي : فالعبد إذا دخل في الصلاة رفع الحجاب , وإذا التفت أرخى , قالك وهو خوف ممزوج بتيقظ واستكانة , ثم قد يكون في المعاملة إيثارا ومجاملة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r11.speaker: ابن كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathīr says khushūʿ comes when the heart is free for prayer, occupied with it over other matters, and prefers it; then prayer becomes rest and delight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن كثير : والخشوع في ا لصلاة إنما يحصل لمن فرغ قلبه لها , واشتغل بها عما عداها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r12.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r12.claim: Anas reports the saying that the Prophet's greatest comfort was placed in prayer; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r12.anchor: وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة ) رواه أحمد والنسائي عن أنس رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r13.speaker: رجل من أسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r13.claim: A man of Aslam reports the Prophet telling Bilāl to give them rest through prayer; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p182#2/r13.anchor: يا بلال ! أرحنا بالصلاة ) - رواه أحمد عن رجل من أسلم رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r9.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r9.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet raised his eyes toward heaven in prayer, after which this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r9.anchor: عن محمد ابن سيرين قال: نبئت أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r10.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r10.claim: A second report from Ibn Sirin says the Prophet looked right and left while standing in prayer; after the verse came down, he bowed his head.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r10.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذا قام في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r11.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r11.claim: Ibn Sirin says the Companions used to raise their eyes and turn during prayer; after the verse, they lowered their heads and stopped looking up or turning.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r11.anchor: عن محمد ابن سيرين قال: كان أصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يرفعون

DURR-FULL:v6p83/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r12.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r12.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet sometimes looked at something in prayer and raised his gaze; when this verse was revealed, he lowered his head.
DURR-FULL:v6p83/r12.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ربما ينظر إلى الشيء

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet raised his eyes toward heaven in prayer and bowed his head when the verse was revealed; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين عن أبي هريرة أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا صلى

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says worshippers faced their prayer, lowered their gaze to the place of prostration, knew God was attending to them, and did not turn aside.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: كانوا إذا قاموا في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r3.claim: Ali locates humility in the heart and also describes it as gentleness toward a Muslim and avoiding turns during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r3.anchor: عن علي أنه سئل عن قوله {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: الخشوع في القلب

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses khushūʿ as fearfulness and stillness.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: خائفون ساكنون

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r5.claim: The Prophet warns against hypocritical humility, defining it as a humble body paired with a hypocritical heart.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r5.anchor: عن أبي بكر الصديق قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - تعوذوا بالله من خشوع النفاق

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda also urges seeking refuge from hypocritical humility, in which the body appears humble while the heart is not.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r6.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: استعيذوا بالله من خشوع النفاق قيل له: وما خشوع النفاق

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r7.claim: Qatada defines humility as fear in the heart and lowering the gaze during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قال: الخشوع في القلب هو الخوف وغض البصر في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r8.claim: Ibrahim says humility is in the heart and also glosses the worshippers as silent.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: الخشوع في القلب وقال: ساكتون

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their eyes and their posture became humble.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: كان خشوعهم في قلوبهم فغضوا

DURR-FULL:v6p84/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r10.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri glosses khushūʿ as a person's stillness during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p84/r10.anchor: عن الزهري {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} قال: هو سكون المرء في صلاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.claim: The repeated relative construction presents each trait as a cause of success because each signals firmly rooted faith; the list need not exhaust piety or every cause of success.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r1.anchor: وبتكريره للإيماء إلى وجه فلاحهم وعلته ، أي أن كل خصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.claim: The contrast with condemned people who did not pray, feed the poor, or heed Judgment shows the traits' causal relevance, though an enumeration need not be exhaustive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r2.anchor: كما كانت أضدادها كذلك في قوله تعالى { ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r3.claim: Khushu is fear that produces reverence; directed to God, it entails piety and contributes to success.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r3.anchor: وهو خوف يوجب تعظيم المخوف منه ، ولا شك أن الخشوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r4.claim: Khushu belongs to the heart rather than being a formal act of prayer and can exist outside prayer, but is singled out in prayer because prayer especially stirs it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r4.anchor: إذ الخشوع محله القلب فليس من أفعال الصلاة ولكنه يتلبس به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r5.claim: Prayer is the most fitting state for khushu because it is intimate address to God, making the worshipper feel before Him; this is foundational conduct toward the Creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r5.anchor: ولأن الخشوع لما كان لله تعالى كان أولى الأحوال به حال الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r6.claim: This attribute comes first after faith because prayer is the foremost setting for khushu, praising believers first for faith and then humility before God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p9/r6.anchor: ولهذا الاعتبار قدم هذا الوصف على بقية أوصاف المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r1.claim: Putting in their prayer before humble emphasizes close attachment to prayer; the possessive construction signals strong connection, unlike saying they are humble whenever they pray.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r1.anchor: وتقديم في صلاتهم } على { خاشعون } للاهتمام بالصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r2.claim: The nominal sentence conveys lasting, stable khushu as a character trait; a verbal expression such as they humbled would not, and the wording is concise without losing force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p10/r2.anchor: ما تدل عليه الجملة الاسمية من ثبات الخشوع لهم ودوامه

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r1.claim: Khushu means fear and humility; the worshippers fear God, humble themselves before Him, and keep their eyes fixed on their prayer places.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r1.anchor: أي خائفون من الله متذللون له ملزمون أبصارهم مساجدهم

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r2.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r2.claim: Al-Mufradat defines khushu as submissiveness, usually visible in bodily limbs, while humility is more often found in the heart.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r2.anchor: في "المفردات" : الخشوع : الضراعة وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r3.claim: A report says that when the heart is submissive, the limbs become humble.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r3.anchor: فيما ورد : "إذا ضرع القلب خشعت الجوارح"

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r4.claim: After this verse descended, the Prophet lowered his gaze toward his place of prostration, having previously looked toward the sky during prayer.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r4.anchor: روي : أنه عليه السلام كان إذا صلى رفع بصره إلى السماء

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r5.claim: The Prophet saw a worshipper playing with his beard and said that a humble heart would make the limbs humble.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r5.anchor: وأنه رأى مصليا يعبث بلحيته فقال : "لو خشع قلب هذا لخشعت جوارحه"

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r6.speaker: النتف
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r6.claim: Al-Nutaf regards looking skyward at the opening takbir as disliked because it is a prohibited turn during prayer; outside prayer it is not disliked, since the sky is the direction of supplication and the source of blessings.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r6.anchor: وفي "النتف" : يكره تقليب الوجه إلى نحو السماء عند التكبيرة الأولى

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r7.claim: Kashifi says the worshipper should look at the prostration place while standing, except in Mecca, where the gaze should fall on the Sacred House.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (رلباب فرموده كه درحالت قيام ديده برسجده كاه بايد نهاد

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r8.claim: A hadith depicts the worshipper standing before the All-Merciful; if he turns away, God asks whom he seeks and calls him back to the better object of attention.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن العبد إذا قام إلى الصلاة فإنما هو بين يدي الرحمن فإذا التفت

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r9.claim: Najmiyya maps outward khushu to bowed head, lowered eyes, attentive ear, present measured tongue, folded hands, level bow, restraint from lustful thoughts, and still feet.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r9.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : خاشعون أي بالظاهر والباطن

BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r10.claim: Inward khushu quiets the soul from passing thoughts, keeps the heart in remembrance and presence, watches over the secret against glancing at created things, and immerses the spirit in love and disclosure of beauty and majesty.
BURSEVI:v6p47#2/r10.anchor: وأما الباطن : فخشوع النفس سكونها عن الخواطر والهواجس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r6.claim: Khushūʿ is bodily lowering, stillness of the limbs, and dignity, and appears in someone whose heart is fearful and humble.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r6.anchor: والخشوع التطامن وسكون الأعضاء والوقار، وهذا إنما يظهر ممن في قلبه خوف واستكانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r7.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r7.claim: A scholar saw a man playing with his beard in prayer and remarked that if his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن بعض العلماء أنه رأى رجلا يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة فقال: لو خشع هذا خشعت جوارحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r8.claim: One occasion report says Muslims used to look right and left during prayer; the verse directed worshippers to look toward the qibla or before them, and in the sanctuary toward the Kaaba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r8.anchor: وروي أن سبب هذه الآية أن المسلمين كانوا يلتفتون في صلاتهم يمنة ويسرة فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r9.speaker: ابن سيرين وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r9.claim: Ibn Sīrīn and others report that the Prophet looked toward heaven in prayer and that the verse was revealed about this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين وغيره أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يلتفت في صلاته إلى السماء فنزلت الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r1.claim: The root sense of khushūʿ is submission and humility.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r1.anchor: وأصل الخشوع في اللغة الخضوع والتواضع وفي المراد بالخشوع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky in prayer; after this verse was revealed, he lowered his head.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r2.anchor: روى أبو هريرة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى رفع بصره إلى السماء فنزلت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r3.speaker: مسلم بن يسار وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r3.claim: They understand humility in prayer as looking toward the place of prostration.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r3.anchor: فنكس رأسه والى هذا المعنى ذهب مسلم بن يسار وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r4.claim: Ali interprets it as refraining from turning during prayer and being gentle toward a Muslim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه ترك الالتفات في الصلاة وأن تلين كنفك للرجل المسلم قاله علي بن أبي طالب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r5.speaker: مجاهد وإبراهيم والزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r5.claim: Mujahid, Ibrahim, and al-Zuhri take humility to mean stillness during prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p459/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه السكون في الصلاة قاله مجاهد وابراهيم والزهري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses khushu as fearful and still; Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Zuhri are also reported to hold this gloss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، إبراهيم النخعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r2.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i define khushu as humility of the heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r2.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه: الخشوع: خشوع القلب. وكذا قال إبراهيم النخعي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r3.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says humility in their hearts led worshippers to lower their eyes and lower their wing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: كان خشوعهم في قلوبهم، فغضوا بذلك أبصارهم، وخفضوا الجناح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin says the Companions used to look toward the sky in prayer, then lowered their gaze to the place of prostration after this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r4.anchor: وقال محمد بن سيرين: كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة، فلما نزلت هذه الآية:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r5.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r5.claim: Ibn Sirin says they advised keeping the gaze within the prayer place and closing the eyes if one was accustomed to looking around.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r5.anchor: قال ابن سيرين: وكانوا يقولون: لا يجاوز بصره مصلاه، فإن كان قد اعتاد النظر فليغمض. رواه ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir also transmits mursal reports from Ibn Sirin and Ata ibn Abi Rabah that the Prophet kept his gaze as described until this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r6.anchor: ثم روى (5) ابن جرير عنه، وعن عطاء بن أبي رباح أيضا مرسلا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يفعل ذلك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r7.claim: Khushu comes from emptying the heart for prayer, attending to it over other concerns, and preferring it; then prayer becomes rest and delight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r7.anchor: والخشوع في الصلاة إنما يحصل بمن فرغ قلبه لها، واشتغل بها عما عداها، وآثرها على غيرها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r8.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying perfume and women were made beloved to him and prayer was made the delight of his eye.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r8.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، في الحديث الذي رواه الإمام أحمد والنسائي، عن أنس، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "حبب إلي الطيب والنساء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r9.speaker: رجل من أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r9.claim: A man from Aslam reports the Prophet telling Bilal to give them rest through prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r9.anchor: وقال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا وكيع، حدثنا مسعر، عن عمرو بن مرة، عن سالم بن أبي الجعد، عن رجل من أسلم، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r10.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya reports an Ansari relative asking for ablution so he could pray and rest, then citing the Prophet's instruction to Bilal to bring rest through prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p461/r10.anchor: وقال الإمام أحمد أيضا؛ حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، حدثنا إسرائيل، عن عثمان بن المغيرة، عن سالم ابن أبي الجعد، أن محمد بن الحنفية قال:

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r11.claim: Khushūʿ originally means stillness and humility; al-Layth distinguishes it from bodily khudūʿ, locating khushūʿ in sight and voice.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r11.anchor: والخشوع: أصله السكون والتذلل، يقال: خشع له وتخشع

JISHUMI:v7p5018/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r12.speaker: الليث
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r12.claim: Al-Layth says khushūʿ concerns sight and voice, whereas khudūʿ concerns the body; khashʿa also names soft ground.
JISHUMI:v7p5018/r12.anchor: إلا أن الخضوع في البدن، والخشوع في البصر والصوت

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.claim: The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما أزال كل شبهة، فذكر صفات المؤمن، فدل أن من كانت صفته ما ذكر

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r6.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الخشوع في الصلاة

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r7.claim: One view holds that khushūʿ is an act of the heart.

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r8.claim: Another view holds that khushūʿ is an act of the bodily limbs.

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r9.claim: The author prefers that khushūʿ involve heart and limbs: prayer requires outward submission and inward reverence and solemnity.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r9.anchor: من أفعالهما، وهو الأولى؛ إذ لا شبهة أن

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.claim: No other required duties are omitted: worship, contracts, and liabilities fall under trusts and covenants; sins fall under avoiding laghw.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.anchor: قلنا: لا؛ لأن جميع ما كلف دخل في الآية؛ لأن جميع ما يجب فعله من العبادات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r6.claim: Humility in prayer is fear in the heart and lowering one’s gaze to the prostration place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r6.anchor: الخشوع في الصلاة : خشية القلب وإلباد البصر عن قتادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r7.claim: Qatāda defines humility as fixing one’s gaze on the prostration place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة : وهو إلزامه موضع السجود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet lowered his gaze to his prayer place after this verse was revealed; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r8.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 717 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r9.claim: A scholar feared the Merciful enough to keep his gaze still and avoid worldly thoughts; another view is focused attention and turning from everything else.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r9.anchor: وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا قام إلى الصلاة هاب الرحمن أن يشد بصره إلى شيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r10.claim: Prayer manners include avoiding gathered clothing, fidgeting, looking around, stretching, yawning, eye-closing, mouth-covering, letting garments hang, cracking joints, interlocking fingers, akhtiṣār, and turning pebbles.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r10.anchor: ومن الخشوع : أن يستعمل الآداب ، فيتوقى كف الثوب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r11.claim: The Prophet told a man fidgeting with his beard that humble hearts make humble limbs; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r11.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 718 ) أنه أبصر رجلا يعبث بلحيته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan rebuked a man asking for a bride from the houris while fidgeting with pebbles, calling him a bad suitor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r12.anchor: ونظر الحسن إلى رجل يعبث بالحصا وهو يقول : اللهم زوجني الحور العين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p177#2/r13.claim: Prayer is attributed to worshippers because they alone benefit; it is their provision and treasure, while God needs and gains nothing from it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni reports that Aisha had al-Muʾminun recited through “they guard their prayers,” then said that this was the Prophet's character.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r3.anchor: روى أبو عمران الجوني قال قيل لعائشة ما كان خلق رسول الله صل الله عليه وسلم ؟

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret khushuʿ as fearfulness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r5.claim: Ibn ʿIsa interprets khushuʿ as humility.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r5.anchor: والثاني : خاضعون ، وهو قول ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r7.claim: Mujahid interprets khushuʿ as lowering the gaze and one's wing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r7.anchor: الرابع : أنه غض البصر ، وخفض الجناح ، قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r8.claim: Another view requires looking at the place of prostration and not letting the gaze pass the prayer place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r8.anchor: الخامس : هو أن ينظر إلى موضع سجوده من الأرض ، ولا يجوز بصره مصلاه ، فقد روي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet raised his eyes heavenward; this verse came down, after which he kept his gaze within the prayer place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r9.anchor: فقد روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يرفع بصره إلى السماء فنزلت : { الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون }

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r10.claim: One account locates khushuʿ in the heart alone, according to al-Hasan and Qatada.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r10.anchor: أحدهما : في القلب خاصة , وهو قول الحسن وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r11.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r11.claim: A second account locates khushuʿ in both heart and sight, also attributed to al-Hasan and Qatada.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p45/r11.anchor: والثاني : في القلب والبصر , وهو قول الحسن وقتادة .

MUQATIL:23:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r2.claim: Humility in prayer means submission: the praying person does not notice who is to his right or left.
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r2.anchor: { الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون } [آية: 2] يقول: متواضعون يعنى إذا صلى لم يعرف من عن يمينه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r1.claim: Humility in prayer is fear in the heart and stillness in the limbs.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r2.claim: Another explanation is to focus fully on prayer and turn away from everything else, keeping the gaze on the place of prostration and avoiding distraction or fidgeting.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ﴾ خائفون بالقلب ساكنون بالجوارح وقيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda defines humility as sincere speech, reverence for the standing, complete certainty, and gathered attention.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r3.anchor: وعن أبى الدرداء هواخلاص المقال وإعظام المقام واليقين التام وجمع الاهتمام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r4.claim: Prayer is attributed to its performers because they alone benefit from it; it is their provision and treasure, while the One worshipped has no need of it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#3/r4.anchor: وأضيفت الصلاة إلى المصلين لا إلى المصلى له لانتفاع المصلى بها وحده وهى عدته وذخيرته

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r7.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky during prayer; after this verse was revealed, he directed his gaze to the place of prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r7.anchor: روى المعتمر عن خالد عن محمد بن سيرين قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينظر إلى السماء في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r8.speaker: هشيم
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r8.claim: In Hushaym's version, Muslims used to look around during prayer; after the verses were revealed, they faced the prayer and looked ahead.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r8.anchor: وفي رواية هشيم: كان المسلمون يلتفتون في الصلاة وينظرون

QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r9.claim: The author refers readers to his discussion in al-Baqara of the ruling on praying toward the direction one looks.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:1-2/r9.anchor: وقد تقدم ما للعلماء في حكم المصلي إلى حيث ينظر في «البقرة» عند قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r1.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussions of khushuʿ's meaning in al-Baqara, including its locus in the heart and the limbs' following the heart as their ruler.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r1.anchor: والخشوع محله القلب فإذا خشع خشعت الجوارح كلها لخشوعه إذ هو ملكها

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r2.claim: A learned man would fear God when standing for prayer, avoiding both wandering his eyes and thinking about worldly matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r2.anchor: وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا أقام الصلاة وقام إليها يهاب الرحمن

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r3.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r3.claim: Ata defines humility in prayer as not fiddling with any part of one's body.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو ألا يعبث بشيء من جسده في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r4.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r4.claim: The Prophet saw a man playing with his beard during prayer and said that if his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble too.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r4.anchor: وأبصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r5.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet said that mercy faces a person who stands to pray, so they should not move pebbles; al-Tirmidhi transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r5.anchor: وقال أبو ذر قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r6.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r6.claim: A poem praises prayer as comprehensive good, in which the limbs submit to God, mercy meets the worshipper, and the worshipper becomes intimate with the Lord if humble.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r6.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ألا في الصلاة الخير والفضل أجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r7.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r7.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni reports that when Aisha was asked about the Prophet's character, she had the people recite this sura through “they carefully maintain,” pointing to the verses as a description of him.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r7.anchor: وروى أبو عمران الجوني قال: قيل لعائشة ما كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r8.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet glanced right and left in prayer but did not turn his neck behind him.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r8.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يلحظ في صلاته يمينا وشمالا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r9.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r9.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik says that while he prayed near the Prophet he sometimes glanced at him; the Prophet returned the look, then looked away when Ka'b turned toward him, and did not order him to repeat the prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r9.anchor: وقال كعب بن مالك في حديثه الطويل: ثم أصلي قريبا منه يعني من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r10.claim: Scholars disagree whether khushuʿ is a prayer obligation or a virtue completing it; the author says the correct view is that it is obligatory and located in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r10.anchor: على قولين. والصحيح الأول، ومحله القلب

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r11.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r11.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit says khushuʿ is the first knowledge to be taken from people; al-Tirmidhi calls the report through Jubayr ibn Nufayr hasan gharīb, and al-Nasa'i also transmits it through Awf ibn Malik with a sound chain.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r11.anchor: وهو أول علم يرفع من الناس قاله عبادة بن الصامت

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r12.speaker: معاوية بن صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r12.claim: Mu'awiya ibn Salih was judged reliable by Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Ahmad, and Abu Zur'a and used by Muslim; Abu Hatim considered him acceptable for recording but not proof, Yahya ibn Ma'in differed, and only Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan is said to have criticized him.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r12.anchor: قلت: معاوية بن صالح أبو عمرو ويقال أبو عمر الحضرمي الحمصي

QASHANI:23:1-11/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:1-11/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:1-11/r2.claim: Humility is the heart's presence in prayer, overcome by awe and reverence at the manifestation of majesty's light.
QASHANI:23:1-11/r2.anchor: في صلاة حضور القلب { خاشعون } باستيلاء الخشية والهيبة عليهم لتجلي نور العظمة

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r1.claim: Some interpreters define khushūʿ through inward acts such as fear and awe.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r1.anchor: فمنهم من جعله من أفعال القلوب كالخوف والرهبة

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r2.claim: Others define it through bodily stillness and not turning away.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r2.anchor: ومنهم من جعله من أفعال الجوارح كالسكون وترك الالتفات

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r3.claim: Rāzī prefers joining both: inward surrender and humility, attention to divine majesty, and a still, lowered gaze without turning right or left.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r3.anchor: منهم من جمع بين الأمرين وهو الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r4.claim: Only bodily khushūʿ can be seen in a person; the heart's state remains invisible.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r4.anchor: ولكن الخشوع الذي يرى على الإنسان ليس إلا ما يتعلق بالجوارح فإن ما يتعلق بالقلب لا يرى

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r5.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r5.claim: They report that Muslims and the Prophet once raised their eyes heavenward in prayer, then after this verse he lowered his gaze and kept it within his prayer place.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r5.anchor: قال : الحسن وابن سيرين كان المسلمون يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r6.claim: Rāzī says khushūʿ is obligatory in prayer, while his later discussion distinguishes spiritual acceptance from legal discharge.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r6.anchor: قلنا إنه عندنا واجب ويدل عليه أمور

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r7.claim: Reflection on the Qurʾān requires grasping its meaning; tarṭīl likewise means pausing over its wonders and meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r7.anchor: والتدبر لا يتصور بدون الوقوف على المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r8.claim: God's command to remember Him is obligatory, and heedlessness contradicts remembrance, so a wholly heedless person cannot be establishing prayer for remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r8.anchor: وظاهر الأمر للوجوب والغفلة تضاد الذكر فمن غفل

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r9.claim: The prohibition against being among the heedless is outwardly prohibitive and therefore supports requiring attentiveness.

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r10.claim: The requirement that intoxicated people know what they say also applies by analogy to a heedless person absorbed in worldly concerns.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r10.anchor: تعليل لنهي السكران وهو مطرد في الغافل المستغرق المهتم بالدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r11.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r11.claim: A Prophetic saying restricts khushūʿ to one who makes himself humble and lowly.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r11.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( إنما الخشوع لمن تمسكن وتواضع )

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r12.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r12.claim: A prayer that fails to restrain its performer from indecency only increases that person in distance from God; a heedless prayer does not restrain.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r12.anchor: من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r13.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r13.claim: The Prophet says that some people who stand in prayer receive only fatigue and exertion, meaning the heedless.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r13.anchor: كم من قائم حظه من قيامه التعب والنصب

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r14.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r14.claim: A person receives from prayer only the portion he comprehends.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r14.anchor: ليس للعبد من صلاته إلا ما عقل

RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r15.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r15.claim: Al-Ghazālī argues that a worshipper converses privately with God, while speech produced in heedlessness is not intimate address.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68/r15.anchor: قال الغزالي رحمه الله : المصلي يناجي ربه

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.claim: Pilgrimage is arduous and disciplines people through hardship whether or not the heart is present, unlike prayer's intended intimate address.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.anchor: وكذا الحج أفعال شاقة ، وفيه من المجاهدة

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.claim: Prayer's remembrance is meant as intimate address to God; mere sounds have no sound purpose, and the tongue must express the heart's supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.anchor: فثبت أن المقصود منه المناجاة وذلك لا يتحقق إلا إذا كان اللسان معبرا عما في القلب

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.claim: Saying guide us to the straight path with a heedless heart illustrates why prayer's recitation must be understood.

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.claim: An oath to thank, praise, and petition someone is not fulfilled by reciting those phrases without intending to address that person; the analogy illustrates heedless prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.anchor: ثم جرت الألفاظ الدالة على هذه المعاني على لسانه في اليوم

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.claim: Bowing and prostration aim at magnifying God; without awareness they would be indistinguishable from prostrating to an idol, leaving only bodily movement.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.anchor: وأما الركوع والسجود فالمقصود منهما التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.claim: Prayer's central place among difficult acts of worship and its role distinguishing faith from unbelief show that its intended intimate address must accompany its outward actions.

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r7.claim: Jurists differ on whether the worshipper at the final salutation intends those present, absent people, or both; if its meaning merits reflection, the opening and glorifications merit it more.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r7.anchor: هل ينوي الحضور أو الغيبة والحضور معا

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r8.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r8.claim: Opponents object that requiring humility and khushūʿ conflicts with juristic consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r8.anchor: واحتج المخالف بأن اشتراط الخضوع والخشوع على خلاف اجتماع الفقهاء

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r9.claim: Rāzī answers that presence is required for acceptance and reward, not for legal discharge that removes the duty to repeat the prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r9.anchor: أن الحضور عندنا ليس شرطا للأجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r10.claim: Returning a borrowed garment properly discharges the obligation but earns praise, while throwing it back contemptuously still discharges it but earns blame; prayer can likewise be formally discharged yet blameworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r10.anchor: فقد خرج عن العهدة واستحق المدح

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r11.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r11.claim: The theologians agree that inward presence is necessary because intention to obey distinguishes prostration to God from an otherwise similar prostration to an idol.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r11.anchor: أما المتكلمون فقد اتفقوا على أنه لا بد من الحضور

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r12.speaker: أبو الليث
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r12.claim: Abū al-Layth says complete recitation avoids grammatical error and is performed reflectively.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r12.anchor: ذكر الفقيه أبو الليث رحمه الله في تنبيه الغافلين

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r13.speaker: بشر الحافي
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r13.claim: Bishr al-Ḥāfī says that whoever lacks khushūʿ has a corrupted prayer, as transmitted by al-Ghazālī from Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r13.anchor: عن بشر الحافي أنه قال : من لم يخشع فسدت صلاته

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r14.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that a prayer without the heart's presence is nearer to punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r14.anchor: وعن الحسن رحمه الله : كل صلاة لا يحضر فيها القلب

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r15.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r15.claim: Muʿādh says that one who deliberately recognizes who is to his right and left while praying has no prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r15.anchor: وعن معاذ بن جبل : من عرف من على يمينه وشماله متعمدا

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r16.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r16.claim: A transmitted Prophetic report says a person may receive only a sixth or tenth of a prayer, and receives only what he comprehends.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r16.anchor: إن العبد ليصلي الصلاة لا يكتب له سدسها ولا عشرها

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r17.speaker: عبد الواحد بن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r17.claim: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd claims scholarly consensus that a person receives from prayer only what he comprehends.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r17.anchor: وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد : أجمعت العلماء على أنه

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r18.claim: Even if jurists broadly allow prayer without this presence, the stricter position of theologians and the scrupulous is safer.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r18.anchor: فهلا أخذت بالاحتياط فإن بعض العلماء اختار الإمامة

RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r19.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r19.claim: One scholar chose to follow the imam to avoid being criticized by al-Shāfiʿī for omitting the Fātiḥa or by Abū Ḥanīfa for reciting it behind the imam.
RAZI-FULL:v23p68#2/r19.anchor: فقال : أخاف إن تركت الفاتحة أن يعاتبني الشافعي

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r1.claim: Inward humility is understood as self-effacement and obedience.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r1.anchor: In relation to one’s inward state, this verse is said to refer to an attitude of self-effacement and obedience (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī quotes a hadith warning that many worshippers receive only toil and weariness from prayer.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī quotes two ḥādīths: “How many a worshipper stands to pray whose share is only toil and weariness,”

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī also quotes a hadith that a servant receives from prayer only what the servant understands.

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r4.speaker: R and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r4.claim: A report says believers first looked up or elsewhere while praying, then after this verse kept their eyes on the place of prostration; some worshippers instead look forward and slightly down.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r4.anchor: before this verse was revealed the believers would look up toward the sky or elsewhere when standing in prayer, and that afterwards (as is common for worshippers to this day) the believers would keep their eyes on the place where they would touch the ground in prostration (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r5.claim: Humility is also interpreted as stillness in prayer or an attitude of fear during prayer.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r5.anchor: That they are humble is also interpreted to refer to the stillness with which one should perform the prayer, or else it refers to an attitude of fear during the prayer (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r6.claim: Khāshiʿ derives from a root evoking lowered eyes as well as bodily lowliness and withering.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r6.anchor: Humble renders khāshiʿ, from a root that evokes the sense of eyes being lowered or cast down and also has the sense of physical lowliness and withering

STUDYQURAN:23:2/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r7.claim: The spiritual tradition treats humility in prayer as essential discipline, tied to virtues outside prayer and contemplation of God’s Qualities and human infirmities.
STUDYQURAN:23:2/r7.anchor: the attainment and maintenance of a state of humility in prayer is an essential part of spiritual discipline; it is intimately connected with the practice of the virtues outside of prayer
