QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r5.claim: Khushūʿ in prayer is the inner self bowed in intimate conversation, complete awe, melting under unveiling, and effacement beneath manifestations.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r5.anchor: والخشوع في الصلاة إطراق السر على بساط النجوى باستكمال نعت الهيبة ، والذوبان تحت سلطان الكشف

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r6.claim: Nearness and perfect intimacy come to one who stands in prayer with awe and observes the etiquette of the divine presence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r6.anchor: أدرك ثمرات القرب وفاز بكمال الأنس من وقف على بساط النجوى بنعت الهيبة ، ومراعاة آداب الحضرة

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r7.claim: Intimacy with the Beloved is complete only when the watcher is absent; the most intrusive watcher is the self.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r7.anchor: ولا يكمل الأنس بلقاء المحبوب إلا عند فقد الرقيب . وأشد الرقباء وأكثرهم تنغيصا لأوان القرب النفس

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r8.claim: When the worshipper withdraws from awareness of the self and its afflictions, life becomes pleasant, blessings complete, and joy apparent.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r8.anchor: فإذا خنس عن نفسه وشاهده عدم إحساسه بآفات نفسه ، وطاب له العيش ، وتمت له النعمى

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r9.claim: Whatever distracts from God is heedlessness; what is merely for oneself is excess, speech not heard from God or understood with Him is vain, and lingering on other than the Real is estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r9.anchor: ما يشغل عن الله فهو سهو ، وما لي لله فهو حشو ، وما ليس بمسموع من الله أو بمعقول مع الله فهو لغو

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r10.claim: Speech by creatures that does not praise and extol God is vain.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r10.anchor: ما ليس بتقريظ الله ومدحه من كلام خلقه فكل ذلك لغو

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r1.claim: Khushuʿ in prayer is humility and submission to God through obedience and carrying out what He commanded in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: «السكون فيها»

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r2.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r2.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky in prayer; after this verse was revealed, he faced the place of prostration.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين، قال: " كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى نظر إلى السماء، فأنزلت هذه الآية: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2]

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r3.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin says the Companions raised their eyes skyward in prayer until this verse came, after which they lowered their heads.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r3.anchor: عن ابن سيرين، قال: " كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرفعون أبصارهم في الصلاة إلى السماء؛ حتى نزلت: {قد أفلح المؤمنون الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2]

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin says he was told the Prophet looked up in prayer and then lowered his gaze; the informant was unsure whether this verse was the one revealed, and reports keeping the gaze on the prayer place.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r4.anchor: وقال محمد: وكانوا يقولون: لا يجاوز بصره مصلاه، فإن كان قد استعاد النظر فليغمض

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r5.claim: Mujahid explains khushuʿ as stillness in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: «السكون فيها»

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r6.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r6.claim: Al-Zuhri likewise defines khushuʿ as a person's stillness during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r6.anchor: عن الزهري: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: سكون المرء في صلاته

TAB-FULL:v17p6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r7.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r7.claim: ʿAli says the worshiper should not turn during prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p6/r7.anchor: عن علي، قال: " سئل عن قوله: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: لا تلتفت في صلاتك "

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes prayerful khushūʿ broadly as humble obedience to God and performance of prescribed worship; its signs are still limbs, attention to duty and leaving what is forbidden, since no evidence restricts it to one sense.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r1.anchor: وإذ كان ذلك كذلك، ولم يكن الله تعالى ذكره دل على أن مراده من ذلك معنى دون معنى في عقل ولا خبر

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r2.speaker: غير عطاء
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r2.claim: A narrator other than ʿAṭāʾ says the Prophet looked around in prayer until this verse came down, after which he looked only toward the ground; the passage also notes that people had raised their eyes toward the sky before revelation.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r2.anchor: وقال لي غير عطاء: " كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام في الصلاة نظر عن يمينه ويساره ووجاهه

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says their humility was in their hearts, so they lowered their gaze and their wing (demeanor).
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: " {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: «كان خشوعهم في قلوبهم، فغضوا بذلك البصر، وخفضوا به الجناح»

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm says khushūʿ is in the heart and means being still.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: " الخشوع في القلب، وقال: ساكنون "

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r5.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r5.claim: ʿAlī says khushūʿ is in the heart, being gentle toward a Muslim, and not turning around.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r5.anchor: عن رجل من قومه، عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: «الخشوع في القلب، وأن تلين للمرء المسلم كنفك، ولا تلتفت»

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ explains it simply as displaying humility in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r6.anchor: قال: ثني حجاج، عن ابن جريج قال: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح في قوله: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: «التخشع في الصلاة»

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r7.claim: Other interpreters take khushūʿ here to mean fear.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: عني به الخوف في هذا الموضع

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the worshippers as fearful.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r8.anchor: حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى، قال: ثنا ابن ثور، عن معمر، عن الحسن: " {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] قال: «خائفون»

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r9.claim: Qatāda says khushūʿ is in the heart.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r9.anchor: قال الحسن: خائفون. وقال قتادة: الخشوع في القلب

TAB-FULL:v17p9/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains them as fearful and still.
TAB-FULL:v17p9/r10.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] يقول: «خائفون ساكنون»

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r1.claim: The humble maintain the proper courtesies of the command, fearing they may lose the blessing of intimate communion.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r1.anchor: قال القاسم في هذه الآية قال : هم المقيمون على شروط آداب الأمر

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r2.claim: Humility is the heart’s abasement within the breast under God’s gaze.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r2.anchor: قال أبو سليمان : الخشوع خشوع القلب ، وذلك ذل القلوب

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r3.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r3.claim: Their hearts, limbs, and aspirations are humbled in prayer through humble communion with God.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r3.anchor: وقال فارس : خشعت قلوبهم ، وجوارحهم ، وهممهم عند الصلاة

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r4.claim: Having seen the sources of the Real’s gifts and the Real’s regard for them, their outward selves became humble.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لما طالعوا موارد الحق عليهم ، ومطالعة الحق إياهم

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r5.claim: A play on humility and pride: they were too proud to be arrogant in prayer, taking pride in resisting pride.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : استكبروا أن يستكبروا في الصلاة لخشوعهم

SULAMI:v2p30#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r6.claim: Their limbs and aspirations shun defilement by created things because their aims are lofty; the anonymous couplet says even their lesser aim surpasses time.
SULAMI:v2p30#4/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : خشعت جوارحهم وهممهم عن التدنس بشيء من الأكوان

TUSTARI:23:1-2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r1.claim: Outward humility is standing before God while observing the command's proper etiquette and purifying movement and stillness from all besides Him; its root is inward fear, which appears outwardly as humility and is a condition of faith.
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r1.anchor: الخشوع علانية، وهو الوقوف بين يدي الله تعالى

TUSTARI:23:1-2/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r2.speaker: الحسن بن علي
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r2.claim: Hasan ibn ʿAli's color changed after ablution; he explained that a person about to enter before the Lord of the Throne ought to change color.
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r2.anchor: وقد حكي عن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنه أنه إذا فرغ من وضوئه

TUSTARI:23:1-2/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Muʿadh that the Qur'an restrains believers from many desires and ruin; they are bound to the truth, striving to free themselves and remaining anxious until they cross Hell's bridge.
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r3.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

TUSTARI:23:1-2/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r4.claim: The Prophet says believers know that watchers record their senses, limbs, and even small acts; piety accompanies them, the Qur'an guides, fear and longing lead, awe marks them, prayer shelters, fasting shields, charity frees, truth serves, modesty commands, and God watches.
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r4.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

TUSTARI:23:1-2/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r5.claim: The Prophet tells Muʿadh that he loves for him what he loves for himself, conveyed what Gabriel conveyed, and hopes to find no one happier on Judgment Day for God's gifts.
TUSTARI:23:1-2/r5.anchor: ويروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لمعاذ

TABATABAI:23:2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:2/r2.claim: Khushu is the subdued person's particular response before an overpowering presence: turning wholly toward it and becoming disconnected from everything else.
TABATABAI:23:2/r2.anchor: الخشوع تأثر خاص من المقهور قبال القاهر بحيث ينقطع عن غيره بالتوجه إليه

TABATABAI:23:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:2/r3.claim: Khushu is primarily a quality of the heart, then attributed figuratively to limbs and other things; the humbled voices before the Merciful illustrate this usage.
TABATABAI:23:2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنه من صفات القلب ثم ينسب إلى الجوارح أو غيرها بنوع من العناية

TABATABAI:23:2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:23:2/r4.claim: A report says that if a man fiddling with his beard in prayer had a humble heart, his limbs would be humble too.
TABATABAI:23:2/r4.anchor: كقوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - على ما روي - فيمن يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة أما إنه لو خشع قلبه لخشعت جوارحه

TABATABAI:23:2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:23:2/r5.claim: Some explain khushu as fear and bodily stillness; others offer lowered eyes or posture, avoiding side glances, reverence, focused attention, or submission, all encompassed by the author's definition.
TABATABAI:23:2/r5.anchor: كقول بعضهم هو الخوف وسكون الجوارح

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.claim: The traits in the opening passage show faith as living and active, producing its effects so that the believer reaches the intended end, success.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية إلى تمام ثماني آيات تذكر من أوصاف المؤمنين ما يلازم كون وصف الإيمان حيا فعالا

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r2.claim: Prayer turns the utterly poor and humble toward majesty and the source of honor; sincere faith unifies concern and absorbs attention, displacing distractions.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r2.anchor: فإن الصلاة توجه ممن ليس له إلا الفقر والذله إلى ساحة العظمة والكبرياء ومنبع العزة والبهاء

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r3.claim: In a report narrated by al-Kafi and other sources through Haritha ibn al-Nu'man, the Prophet says every truth has a reality and every right thing a light.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r3.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في حديث الحارثة بن النعمان المروي في الكافي وغيره إن لكل حق حقيقة ولكل صواب نورا

TABATABAI:23:8-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r8.claim: Prayer is singular with khushu because humility applies uniformly to the genus of prayer, but plural with maintenance because the individual obligatory prayers must all be guarded.
TABATABAI:23:8-11/r8.anchor: لأن الخشوع في جنس الصلاة على حد سواء فلا موجب لجمعها

TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r1.claim: Al-Majma reports that the Prophet saw a man fiddling with his beard in prayer and said a humble heart would make the limbs humble; al-Durr al-Manthur also cites this from several compilers, with no grading stated.
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r1.anchor: في المجمع في الآية روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم رأى رجلا يعبث بلحيته في صلاته

TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r2.claim: Al-Majma reports that the Prophet used to look heavenward in prayer, then lowered his head and gaze after this verse was revealed; al-Durr al-Manthur also cites it from several compilers, without a stated grading.
TABATABAI:23:1-11#3/r2.anchor: وفيه روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يرفع بصره إلى السماء في صلاته فلما نزلت الآية

TABRISI:23:1-3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
TABRISI:23:1-3/r2.claim: Kufan readers except Asim read prayer singular; the remaining readers use plural.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r2.anchor: وقرأ على صلاتهم بالأفراد أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون على صلواتهم على الجمع

TABRISI:23:1-3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:23:1-3/r5.claim: Singular prayer is a verbal noun; plural treats it as a name for distinct kinds and is stronger as a legal term incorporating additions absent from the original language.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r5.anchor: ووجه الإفراد في الصلاة أنها مصدر ووجه الجمع أنها بمنزلة الاسم لاختلاف أنواعها

TABRISI:23:1-3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:1-3/r10.claim: Humility means submission and modesty, keeping the gaze at prostration and not looking to either side.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r10.anchor: أي خاضعون متواضعون متذللون لا يرفعون أبصارهم عن مواضع سجودهم

TABRISI:23:1-3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r11.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:23:1-3/r11.claim: The Prophet saw a man playing with his beard in prayer and said that a humble heart would make the limbs humble too.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r11.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى رجلا يعبث بلحيته في صلاته

TABRISI:23:1-3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:1-3/r12.claim: Inward humility focuses the heart on worship and God; outward humility lowers the gaze, attends to prayer, and avoids turning and fidgeting.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r12.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن الخشوع في الصلاة يكون بالقلب وبالجوارح

TABRISI:23:1-3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:23:1-3/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the humble worshipper is unaware of who is to the right or left.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: خشع فلا يعرف من على يمينه ولا من على يساره

TABRISI:23:1-3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:1-3/r14.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:23:1-3/r14.claim: The Prophet used to look at the sky in prayer; after this verse he lowered his head and looked at the ground.
TABRISI:23:1-3/r14.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يرفع بصره إلى السماء في صلاته

THALABI:v7p37#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p37#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains humility in prayer as being submissive and humbled.

THALABI:v7p37#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
THALABI:v7p37#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret humility in prayer as fearfulness.

THALABI:v7p37#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r7.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p37#3/r7.claim: Muqatil says humility is inward reverence expressed in gentle conduct toward Muslims and by not turning the gaze around.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r7.anchor: مقاتل: متواضعون على الخشوع في القلب، وأن تلين للمرء المسلم كنفك ولا تلتفت

THALABI:v7p37#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p37#3/r8.claim: Mujahid defines humility as lowering the eyes and being deferential; the learned feared God and avoided looking about or dwelling on worldly concerns in prayer.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r8.anchor: مجاهد: هو غض البصر وخفض الجناح وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا قام إلى الصلاة هاب الرحمن

THALABI:v7p37#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r9.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
THALABI:v7p37#3/r9.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says humility is not simply bowing and prostrating, but stillness and dignified bearing in prayer.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r9.anchor: عمرو بن دينار: ليس الخشوع الركوع والسجود ولكنه السكون وحسن الهيئة في الصلاة.

THALABI:v7p37#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p37#3/r10.speaker: ابن سيرين وغيره
THALABI:v7p37#3/r10.claim: Ibn Sirin and others say the worshipper should not lift the gaze from the place of prostration.
THALABI:v7p37#3/r10.anchor: ابن سيرين وغيره: هو أن لا ترفع بصرك عن موضع سجودك.

THALABI:v7p38/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p38/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet and Companions looked toward the sky and around in prayer before this verse; afterward they faced the prostration place and looked down.
THALABI:v7p38/r1.anchor: قالوا: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه يرفعون أبصارهم في الصلاة إلى السماء وينظرون يمينا ويسارا حتى نزلت هذه الآية

THALABI:v7p38/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r2.speaker: ربيع
THALABI:v7p38/r2.claim: Rabi‘ defines humility in prayer as not turning right or left.
THALABI:v7p38/r2.anchor: ربيع: هو أن لا يلتفت يمينا ولا شمالا.

THALABI:v7p38/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v7p38/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a worshipper faces God’s attention; if he looks away, God asks whom he seeks and calls him back to prayer.
THALABI:v7p38/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ان العبد إذا قام إلى الصلاة فإنه بين عيني الرحمان عز وجل فإذا التفت قال له الرب

THALABI:v7p38/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r4.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v7p38/r4.claim: Ata says humility means not fidgeting with any part of the body during prayer.
THALABI:v7p38/r4.anchor: عطاء: هو أن لا تعبث بشيء من جسدك في الصلاة،

THALABI:v7p38/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r5.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v7p38/r5.claim: When the Prophet saw a man playing with his beard during prayer, he said that a humble heart would make the limbs humble too.
THALABI:v7p38/r5.anchor: وأبصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة فقال: لو خشع قلب هذا خشعت جوارحه .

THALABI:v7p38/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v7p38/r6.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying mercy faces the person who stands to pray, so he should not move pebbles.
THALABI:v7p38/r6.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا قام أحدكم إلى الصلاة فإن الرحمة تواجهه فلا يحركن الحصى

THALABI:v7p38/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r7.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p38/r7.claim: Al-Hasan rebuked a man who asked God for a wife among the houris while playing with pebbles, calling him a bad suitor.
THALABI:v7p38/r7.anchor: ويقال: نظر الحسن إلى رجل يعبث بالحصى ويقول: اللهم زوجني من الحور العين، فقال: بئس الخاطب أنت

THALABI:v7p38/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r8.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p38/r8.claim: Qatada defines humility as placing the right hand over the left in prayer.
THALABI:v7p38/r8.anchor: خليد بن دعلج عن قتادة: هو وضع اليمين على الشمال في الصلاة.

THALABI:v7p38/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r9.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p38/r9.claim: Some say humility consists of gathering one’s full attention for prayer and turning away from everything else.
THALABI:v7p38/r9.anchor: بعضهم: هو جمع الهمة لها والإعراض عما سواها.

THALABI:v7p38/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p38/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
THALABI:v7p38/r10.claim: Abu Bakr al-Wasiti describes humility as praying sincerely for God without seeking compensation.
THALABI:v7p38/r10.anchor: أبو بكر الواسطي: هو الصلاة لله سبحانه على الخلوص من غير عوض.

THALABI:v7p39/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p39/r1.claim: The continuation of the quoted saying lists four conditions for humility: reverence, sincere speech, complete certainty, and focused aspiration.
THALABI:v7p39/r1.anchor: إعظام المقام، وإخلاص المقال، واليقين التمام، وجمع الهمة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r1.speaker: الزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri defines khushu in prayer as a person’s stillness; the Arabic root sense is stillness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r1.anchor: قال الزهري (¬4): هو سكون المرء في صلاته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r2.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the worshippers as humble; Mujahid and Ibrahim say still; Amr ibn Dinar says stillness and good bearing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r2.anchor: فقال السدي: متواضعون (¬8). وقال مجاهد وإبراهيم: ساكنون (¬9). وقال عمرو بن دينار: هو السكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret khushu as fear; the author says fear explains the stillness caused by fear of God rather than defining the word itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: خائفون (¬2). وهذا معنى؛ لأن (¬3) من سكن في صلاته إنما هو لخوفه من الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r4.claim: Lowering the gaze and lowering oneself also express khushu, but both reduce to stillness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the worshipper is so fearful of God that he does not know who is to his right or left.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r5.anchor: يدل عليه ما روي عن ابن عباس -في هذه الآية- قال: خشع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky during prayer until this verse came down; afterward he looked where he prostrated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p520#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين قال: كان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- إذا صلى نظر في السماء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r2.claim: Their humility in prayer means being still and keeping their eyes lowered to the place of prostration.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r2.anchor: ساكنون لا يرفعون ابصارهم عن مواضع سجودهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r4.claim: Hasan explains humility in prayer as fear firmly settled in the heart.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال: الخشوع: الخوف الثابت في القلب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r5.claim: Mujahid explains humility as lowering the gaze and being gentle and subdued.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الخشوع: غض البصر وخفض الجناح

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says scholars disliked fidgeting with the hands, looking around, or occupying the mind with worldly matters during prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان أهل العلم يكرهون إذا قام الرجل في صلاته أن يعبث بشيء

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r7.claim: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud prayed with lowered gaze, hands, and voice.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة أن عبد الله بن مسعود كان إذا قام في الصلاة خفض فيها بصره

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r8.claim: Ibn Sirin says people used to look around in prayer until this verse came down, after which they lowered their eyes and seemed to look at the place of prostration.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال: كانوا يلتفتون في صلاتهم حتى نزلت هذه الآية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r9.claim: Hasan also glosses the humble as fearful.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p392#2/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: {الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون} [المؤمنون: 2] أي خائفون

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r4.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r4.claim: Some define khushu as an inward act of the heart, such as fear and awe.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r4.anchor: bazıları “havf” ve[^2]“rehbet” gibi kalb fiillerinden olmak üzere târif etmiş

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r5.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r5.claim: Others define khushu through bodily acts, such as stillness and refraining from looking around.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r5.anchor: bazıları da sükûn ve terk-i iltifat gibi cevârih fiillerinden göstermiştir.

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r6.claim: Elmalılı prefers a combined account: khushu originates in the heart and appears in the body.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r6.anchor: Doğrusu “huşû‘”, aslı kalbde, tezahürü bedende olmak üzere ikisini de câmi‘dir.

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r7.claim: Inwardly it is profound reverence before divine majesty, making the self submit to God's command and attend only to reverence and propriety.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r7.anchor: azamet ve celâl-i rabbânî karşısında kendi küçüklüğünü göstererek nefsi emr-i Hakk’a serfürû ettirecek ve edeb ü tâzimden başka bir hâtıraya iltifat etmeyecek

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r8.claim: Outwardly it produces calm limbs and gaze directed to the place of prostration, without looking to either side or at distractions.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r8.anchor: a‘zâ-yı bedende bu hissin tezahürüyle bir sükûn ve sekînet hâsıl olması ve gözlerinin önüne secde mevzi‘ine bakıp sağa sola

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r9.claim: The inward root of khushu relates to perfecting the intention, a condition of prayer; its outward display relates to prayer's manners and refinements.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r9.anchor: huşû‘un aslı, namazın şartlarından olan niyetin kemâliyle, tezâhürâtı da namazın âdâb ve mükemmilâtıyla alâkadardır.

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r10.speaker: Hasan ve İbn Sîrîn
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r10.claim: Hasan and Ibn Sirin report that the Messenger and Companions once raised their eyes skyward in prayer, then lowered them after this verse and stopped ihtisar.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r10.anchor: Hasan’dan ve İbn Sîrîn’den rivayet olunduğuna göre Resûlullah ve ashâbı namazda gözlerini semâya kaldırırlardı, bu âyetin nüzûlü üzerine önlerine eğdiler ve ıhtisârı terk ettiler.

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r11.speaker: Hazret-i Aişe
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r11.claim: Aisha reports in al-Bukhari and Muslim that the Prophet called looking around in prayer a snatching by Satan from the servant's prayer.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r11.anchor: Buhârî ve Müslim’de Hazret-i Aişe’den de rivayet olunur ki; “Resûlullah’a namazda iltifattan sual ettim

ELMALILI:23:1-2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r12.speaker: Ümm-i Rûman
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r12.claim: Umm Ruman recounts Abu Bakr rebuking her for rocking in prayer, then citing the Prophet that worshippers should be still and not rock like Jews, since still limbs complete prayer.
ELMALILI:23:1-2/r12.anchor: Ümm-i Rûman radıyallahu anhâ demiştir ki: “Namazımda sallanıyordum, Ebû Bekir radıyallahu anh gördü, beni öyle bir azarladı ki az daha namazdan çıkacaktım.

MAJAZ:v2p55/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p55/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p55/r1.claim: The worshippers are humble: their eyes do not look upward or glance around, and they remain bowed.
MAJAZ:v2p55/r1.anchor: في صلاتهم خاشعون» (2) أي لا تطمح أبصارهم ولا يلتفتون مكبون..

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r1.claim: The author renders khushūʿ as deep reverence and identifies prayer and reverence as two conditions of salvation, with reverence emphasized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r1.anchor: Namazda derin saygı hali yaşamak” kurtuluşun imandan sonraki ilk şartı olarak gösterilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r2.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari explains khushūʿ as the servant displaying obedience and respect for God by praying and fulfilling His command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r2.anchor: Taberî buradaki huşû kelimesini, “kulun namaz kılarak Allah’a itaatini, saygısını sergilemesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r3.claim: Prayer is a foundational expression of turning to God, but bodily acts and recitation alone cannot give it spiritual depth; they must unite with inward servitude and awareness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r3.anchor: bedensel hareketler, dilin âyet ve duaların lafızlarını okuması yeterli değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r4.claim: The Qur’anic vocabulary for worship’s inward and spiritual dimension includes khushūʿ and taqwā.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r4.anchor: Kur’an dilinde huşû, takvâ gibi terimlerle ifade edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r5.claim: Khushūʿ also has theological and moral force: a disbeliever cannot reverently turn to God, and worship without belief or respect is hypocrisy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r5.anchor: Allah’a inanmayanın O’na huşû ile yönelmesi beklenemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r6.claim: Hypocrisy is a mismatch between inner and outer life, essence and speech, making it a profound moral corruption and lack of virtue.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r6.anchor: Münafıklık ise dinî konularda için ve dışın, özün ve sözün birbirine uymamasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r7.claim: For worship to lead to salvation, both its outward form and inward content matter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:2/r7.anchor: ibadetin kurtuluşa götürebilmesi için hem formunun hem de içeriğinin önemine işaret edilmiş bulunmaktadır

NAHHAS:v3p109/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p109/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p109/r2.claim: الذين is nominative as an adjective of المؤمنون; هم في صلاتهم خاشعون is a subject and predicate within the relative clause, as are the following clauses.
NAHHAS:v3p109/r2.anchor: في موضع رفع نعت للمؤمنين ( هم في صلاتهم خاشعون ) مبتدأ وخبره داخلون في الصلة وكذلك ما بعده

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة، ابن سيرين
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r1.claim: Reports say the Prophet raised his gaze to heaven, looked around, or moved his eyes during prayer; after this verse was revealed he lowered his head. Ibn Sirīn's version is mursal.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r1.anchor: أخرج الحاكم عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا صلى رفع بصره إلى السماء فنزلت

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r2.claim: Ibn Sirīn reports mursal that the Companions used to raise their eyes to heaven during prayer, and this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p151#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن سيرين مرسلا كان الصحابة يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة فنزلت

ITQAN:v2p322/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p322/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p322/r1.claim: Khashi‘un means fearful and still or quiet.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.claim: Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.anchor: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يقول

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet raised his gaze toward heaven while praying, and this verse was then revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا صلى رفع بصره

DAMGHANI:v1p157/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p157/r5.claim: In prayer, khushūʿ is stillness of the limbs and directing one's gaze to the place of prostration.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p276/r4.anchor: والثاني : سكون الجوارح . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r4.claim: Khushūʿ means humility of the heart and stillness of the limbs; it is the spirit of prayer, which without it is only a body without a soul.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p129/r4.anchor: والخشوع في الصلاة، يعني خشية القلب وسكون الجوارح، وهو روح الصلاة، والصلاة من غير خشوع، جسد بلا روح.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r5.claim: Khushūʿ itself combines action—gathering attention, humbling the heart, reflection, and fear—with abstention from movement and distraction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r5.anchor: والحق أن الخشوع أمرٌ يجمع بين الفعل والترك، ففيه من الفعل جمع الهمة وتذلل القلب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r6.speaker: التفسير الكبير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r6.claim: Al-Tafsir al-Kabir describes inward submission and exclusive reverence, with a still, lowered gaze and no turning to either side.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p134/r6.anchor: جاء في (التفسير الكبير) : "فالخاشع في صلاته، لا بد وأن يحصل له مما يتعلق بالقلب نهاية الخضوع والتذلل للمعبود.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r5.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r5.claim: Ruh al-Maʿani says beginning and ending with prayer honors it, and beginning with humility highlights that prayer without it is like a body without a spirit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r5.anchor: جاء في (روح المعاني) : "وفي تصدير الأوصاف وختمها بأمر الصلاة تعظيم لشأنها. وتقديم الخشوع للاهتمام به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r6.claim: The opening mention of humility may signal the first quality to be removed, while the closing command to preserve prayer signals what remains last.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p150/r6.anchor: فقد بدأ بالخشوع في الصلاة، وكأنه إشارة إلى أول ما يرفع، وختم بالمحافظة عليها إشارة إلى آخر ما يبقى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.claim: The commands to bow, prostrate, worship, do good, establish prayer and give zakat match the opening of al-Muʾminun and its listed believer qualities.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.anchor: فأنت ترى من الأمر بالركوع والسجود وعبادة الله، وفعل الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.claim: Imperative acts such as bowing, prostration, prayer and zakat become stable believer traits, expressed through nominal descriptions of humility, turning from idle talk and giving zakat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.anchor: فاتصفوا بما أمرهم به ربهم على وجه الثبات، فوصفهم بالصيغة الاسمية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r2.claim: Prayer is faith's foremost manifestation; faith that produces no prayer is barren, useful only as fuel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r2.anchor: The foremost manifestation of faith is the prayer. Faith which does not yield the prayer is like a barren tree that can only be used to ignite fire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r3.claim: Humility of heart is prayer's real essence; prayer without it has no effect on a person's life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r3.anchor: The real essence of the prayer is humility of the heart.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r4.claim: Humble prayer restrains evil, vulgarity, and futile conduct; awareness of God's companionship in prayer protects a person from unbefitting acts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r4.anchor: The prayer punctuated with humility stops a person from evil, vulgarity and useless activities. A person acquires God’s companionship in the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.claim: The next sūrah, al-Nūr, supplements this one: faith illuminating the inner self brightens individual and collective life, while its absence darkens both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.anchor: Details of all these points will be found in the next sūrah: Sūrah al-Nūr which is the supplement of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.claim: Islahi summarizes the earlier passage as a progression from inward faith through prayer, zakāh, restraint, fidelity, and guarded prayer to lasting success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.anchor: on them depends the success of the believers.
